simple.meaning: רֶתֶם (rethem) is a Hebrew word meaning “the Spanish broom (from its pole-like stems).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: רֶתֶם (H7574) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 1 Kings 19:4, with occurrences in 1 Kings, Job, Psalms.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רֶתֶם (H7574) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in רֶתֶם (H7574) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: רֶתֶם (rethem) / H7574 is traced through 1 Kings 19:4, 1 Kings 19:5, Job 30:4, Psalms 120:4 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: the Spanish broom (from its pole-like stems)
definitions.full: H7574. rethem or rothem רֹ֫תֶם noun masculine 1Kin 19:5 a kind of broom-shrub, broom-plant, retem (Late Hebrew id. ; Arabic (on form Lag BN 152); רִיתְמָא ᵑ7 , all = Biblical Hebrew); — absolute ׳ר אֶחָד 19:5 , ׳ר אחת V:4 Kt ( אֶחָד Qr); plural לַחְמָם רְתָמִים שֹׁרֶשׁ Job 30:4 (on text see Bu Che below); רְתָמִים גַּחֲלֵי Psa 120:4 , Rob BR i. 84, 203, 205, 500 Löw No. 313 Post Hastings, DB 'Juniper' Che Ency. Bib. 'Juniper' .

occurrences.englishText: But he himself went a day’s journey into the wilderness, and came and sat down under a juniper tree. Then he requested for himself that he might die, and said, “It is enough. Now, O Yahweh, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers.”
He lay down and slept under a juniper tree; and behold, an angel touched him, and said to him, “Arise and eat!”
They pluck salt herbs by the bushes.
